question: Does price-center migration add context to a closing discount, or is this just generic decline/rebound? Does closing discount repair, state failure or short fixed horizon define profitable ownership?
exploratory_origin: EX053 center_below fixed3 full88.83/DD9.90,comparison87.68/DD9.91,near but fails strict91.58/7.25 goals; center_above loses22.65%. This revealed discount interaction, not proof of new mechanism. New contrasts declared before new results.
comparisons: below only vs existingC5303 and falling_below isolates migration context
center_below process/reversal vs existingC5303 tests process exits
repair vs repair_or_reversal vs fixed3 distinguishes completion of local discount from loss of favorable state
fixed_guard vs existingC5303 tests earlier state-failure cut with same maximum3intentdays
first_below and step_below vs existingC5303 tests need for fresh/ongoing migration
late center_below vs EX049 BP and C5209 same start
rules: Closing discount=log adjusted close<adjusted median8barclose. No RSI, drawdown percentile, prior loss or downtrend requirement. Falling_below removes positive3center gain. Repair exits when closing price>=current center; repair_or_reversal also exits nonpositive3center gain. Fixed_guard exits usual daily center failure or age3. Other rules unchanged; MARKET_INTENT nonfixed exits rearm only on positive centerstep.
objectives: Unchanged MANDATE/3, all goals separately; no center qualification claim; defaultfee.001,cash100000,434/415,separateaccounts,sameexecution.
limits: Adaptive selection from repeated development. If below-only/falling control explains advantage, report generic reversion and do not market it as distinct continuation mechanism. Current account differences not causal participant claims.
next: If interaction survives complete controls, test representative scales and largest losses with explicit alternative; if false, retain narrower conclusion and reframe research.
